SMTO-CTX-0013 — SMTO gave two different places to keep reading a file

GUID: e14f2183-9255-4335-ad37-a3dc889cc1df
Slug: context-read-conflicting-position
Domain: CTX · Subsystem: ctx

What happened

  • SMTO was reading a file you attached in parts, but it pointed to two different places to continue from, so the read was refused. Nothing was read and the file is unchanged.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Let the task keep going for a step or two. SMTO sees this message and usually continues from the place the last read ended.
  2. If it repeats, tell SMTO in the conversation: "Continue reading the attached file from where the last part ended." One clear starting point is all the read needs.
  3. If it still gets stuck, tell SMTO: "Read the attached file again from the beginning." Starting over gives SMTO a fresh, matching place to continue from.

What success looks like

  • SMTO's next steps show the next part of the attached file.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't re-attach or edit the file; it isn't the problem.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A read_context call supplied a continuation cursor and an explicit byte offset that point to different positions in the same source (conflicting_position).

What this means

  • The decoded continuation cursor and an explicitly supplied byte offset point to different positions in the same source. Context admission, storage and reading are separate from executing a tool mutation. Preserve existing task state and receipts; a context diagnostic does not authorize replay of earlier operations.

Why this can happen

  • The decoded continuation cursor and an explicitly supplied byte offset point to different positions in the same source.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the explicit offset with the position represented by next_cursor; retain the cursor returned for this source revision.

How to fix it

  • Continue with next_cursor alone, or pass an offset equal to the cursor's decoded position (native/context_reads.py read_source).
  • Continue with next_cursor alone, or use a matching explicit byte offset.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The next page begins at the prior page's returned continuation position.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Context admission, storage and reading are separate from executing a tool mutation. Preserve existing task state and receipts; a context diagnostic does not authorize replay of earlier operations.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
